title: 1961 AHSME Problem 16
statement: An altitude \(h\) of a triangle is increased by a length \(m.\) How much must be taken from the corresponding base \(b\) so that the area of the new triangle is one-half that of the original triangle?

solutions.text:
If \(t\) is removed, the new area condition is \[ \frac12(b-t)(h+m)=\frac12\left(\frac12bh\right). \] Hence \(b-t=\frac{bh}{2(h+m)},\) so \[ \begin{aligned} t&=b-\frac{bh}{2(h+m)}\\ &=\frac{b(2m+h)}{2(h+m)}. \end{aligned} \]

Therefore, the correct answer is E.
hints: Let \(t\) be the amount removed, so the new base is \(b-t\)
Set \(\frac12(b-t)(h+m)\) equal to half the original area
